role: Data Science Expert (Domain Models) - Data Labs
company_profile: SAP builds enterprise business software used across finance, procurement and supply chain, and its Application AI team builds the semantic context layer that grounds SAP's AI agents in business data.
title: Data Science Expert
summary: Data scientist with 8+ years taking ML and LLM systems from prototype to production across Healthcare, Telecom and AIOps, with an MSc in Machine Learning and AI. Builds RAG pipelines, embeddings and vector database retrieval, and LangGraph multi-agent systems grounded in enterprise data, with automated evaluation and observability. Works in Python, SQL, PySpark and Databricks, translating ambiguous business problems into production AI with stakeholders. Alongside this, I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD.

experience_edits.new: Engineered a production multi-agent chatbot in LangGraph with tool use and multi-turn reasoning over AARP medical-plan data, answering business questions with PySpark analysis and live charts, cutting manual analysis by 98%.

project.name: Business Process Knowledge Graph
bullets: Built a knowledge graph of business entities and order-to-cash process steps in ArangoDB, linking ERP master data to documents so a LangGraph agent could answer questions grounded in both.
Evaluated graph-plus-vector retrieval against plain RAG with LLM evaluators on curated question sets, and served the agent through FastAPI in Docker with tracing.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Data Science Expert role in Data Labs. Much of my recent work is the problem your team describes: making AI agents accurate by grounding them in real business data rather than surface patterns. From telecom alarms to healthcare lab documents, the thread has been retrieval and context a model can rely on.

SAP holds the process data behind order-to-cash, procurement and finance for a large share of global commerce, and building the semantic layer on top of it is the most interesting grounding problem I can think of. My fiancée lives in Berlin, and we plan to move to Munich together and settle in Germany long term.

I would bring RAG and agent engineering that has already run in production. At United Health Group I built a LangGraph multi-agent chatbot over medical-plan data that cut manual analysis by 98%, and at Viavi a RAG assistant that reached a 90% match rate against existing solutions. Ontology design is where I would grow fastest, building on my graph and retrieval work.

Outside work I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD. Teachers only keep using a tool whose answers they can trust, and I hold enterprise agents to the same standard. I would welcome a conversation about the role.
